name: Bremen Airport
before:
Bremen's airport, only 3.5 km south of the city, which makes it one of the easiest arrivals in northern Germany. It handled 1.81 million passengers in 2023, mostly on European city and leisure routes.

The tram is the reason to like it. Line 6 runs every 6 to 10 minutes and reaches the city centre in 11 minutes and the main station in 16.

There is a catch for Ryanair passengers. Ryanair does not use the main terminal at all. It uses Terminal E, a more basic building to the west with its own check-in counters and walk-boarding onto the apron, so point clients at the right building.

The main terminal covers Terminals 1, 2 and 3 with five jet bridge stands.

Inside the airport, the Bremenhalle is a small aviation and space museum displaying the Junkers W33 Bremen and the first Spacelab module. An Airbus plant next door makes aircraft flaps and works on A350 wings, served by Beluga transport flights.
after:
Bremen's airport, only 3.5 km south of the city, which makes it one of the easiest arrivals in northern Germany. It handled just under 2 million passengers in 2025, almost all on flights within Germany and Europe.

The tram is the reason to like it: line 6 runs from the airport across the city to the university. BSAG, the tram operator, says a new line 9 will run via the main station to the airport from 21 March 2027, with line 6 continuing at least every 20 minutes.
